title: Turbocharger Bypass Solenoid Circuit Intermittent (v2)
shortDescription: Turbo bypass solenoid feedback drops in and out under load.
fullDescription: Turbo bypass solenoid feedback drops in and out under load. The boost-control family shares PCM low-side drivers, so a single shorted solenoid sets several neighbor codes at once.
safetyImpact: Boost overshoot can shatter compressor wheels or burst charge pipes.

causes.cause: Stuck wastegate / VGT vanes carboned up
Cracked charge-air pipe causing boost leak

fixSteps.title: Smoke-test the charge-air system
fixSteps.instruction: Pressurize the intake tract to 10-15 psi with a smoke machine. Any visible smoke at couplers, intercooler, or charge pipes is the leak.

fixSteps.title: Actuate the wastegate / VGT
fixSteps.instruction: Use bidirectional control to sweep the actuator full range. The arm must move freely without binding through its stroke.

fixSteps.title: Test the boost solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Bench-test the solenoid for clean click and air-flow change. Resistance must match factory spec, typically 25-35 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the turbo
fixSteps.instruction: Check shaft play and oil return condition. Excessive radial play or oil in the intake means CHRA replacement.

faq.q: Can I drive with limp mode?
faq.a: Limp mode protects the engine but stresses the clutch and transmission. Keep trips short until repaired.

faq.q: Is a tune at fault?
faq.a: Aggressive tunes can overshoot boost targets and trip these codes. Revert to stock and re-test.
